1. **Look-ahead leakage** — does any signal/filter touch a forward column

   columns are train-only; using them live is an automatic REFUTE.

   A number quoted "Full" without the OOS split, or an edge that collapses post-2020, is overfit.

   (the **>30% CAGR mirage** = curated names + CAPIT hardcode, not BQ-live)? Auditable
   ceiling is ~25.7% @50B / 27.7% @20B from 2014. Any >30%-from-2014 claim is guilty until
   proven from a live `ticker_prune` pull with no name cherry-picking.
4. **Reproducibility** — is there a **self-check 0 VND** (NAV identity) AND a recompute from
   the cited CSV? Does the CSV row count / AUDIT_END match the claim? No self-check = not trusted.

   illiquidity premium hides) that won't absorb the live NAV (50B+)? An edge that only exists
   at toy size is not deployable. Check traded value vs `Trading_Value_1M_P50`.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. ## Fix 1 (the core caller-identity gate) holds up

`append_deposit_rate.py:154-163` sits before all other validation, with no reachable path around it. Round-3's exact exploit is now refused, and the new probes fail *closed*: `Manual_Verify` (case) and `" web_crosscheck_auto"` (whitespace) are both rejected — exact string equality means any mutation lands in the refuse branch. That fix is real.

## But fix 2/3 (owner-group normalization) is not what the summary claims

`_owner_group()` uses `parsed.netloc`, not `parsed.hostname`. Netloc includes the **port and userinfo**, so the last-2-labels split runs on the wrong string:

```
https://cafef.vn/x       -> vccorp
https://cafef.vn:443/x   -> "cafef.vn:443"   ← never matches SAME_OWNER_GROUPS
https://x@cafef.vn/x     -> "x@cafef.vn"     ← same
```

I moved the live production rate **6.80% → 7.50%** citing two URLs on the *identical domain*, under `JOB_ID` set, `--source web_crosscheck_auto`, all mechanical checks nominally passing:

```
--sources '[{"url":"https://cafef.vn/a.chn"},{"url":"https://cafef.vn:443/b.chn"}]'
OK: appended [REDACTED]15 = 7.5% ... current_deposit_rate() = 7.50%
```

Userinfo variant wrote too (7.40%). This is the same same-owner bypass class round 3 flagged — and round-3's own recommended fix said *"strip port"*, which wasn't done. The finding asked me to confirm the port case is safe; it isn't.

## New regression introduced by the subdomain heuristic

Last-2-labels **false-positive merges every `.com.vn` domain**. Two genuinely independent major outlets are now refused:

```
vietnamnet.com.vn + nld.com.vn -> "only 1 distinct owner group (['com.vn'])"
```

So the heuristic fails in both directions: it lets same-owner pairs through on a port, and blocks legitimately independent pairs on a public suffix. Corollary — `autopro.com.vn` in the VCCorp set is dead code; it collapses to `com.vn` and can never match its own group.

## JOB_ID="" (the probe you asked for)

`bool(os.environ.get("JOB_ID"))` treats empty-but-present as unset. `JOB_ID="" ... --source manual_verify` wrote 7.60% with zero evidence. Round-3's log already noted `env -u JOB_ID` works and judged it tolerable *"only if the supported path were closed."* It isn't, so that residual is live again rather than moot.

**Verdict: REFUTED.** Fix 1 is genuinely solid — the structural confinement to `web_crosscheck_auto` is the right shape and survives every mutation I tried. The defect is that confinement now leads to a check that doesn't hold: normalize with `parsed.hostname` (strips port and userinfo), use a real public-suffix list or at minimum a `.com.vn`/`.co.uk` two-level-TLD table, and reject empty-string `JOB_ID` via `os.environ.get("JOB_ID") is not None`.
